---
title: A fixture quick start
description: Two shells, one file, and two output blocks, for the extractor and the runner to work on.
quickstart: true
---

import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## Make a working directory

<Tabs syncKey="os">
<TabItem label="Linux and macOS">

```bash
mkdir work && cd work
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Windows PowerShell">

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory work | Out-Null
Set-Location work
```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Write the schema

Put the shape you want in `schema.sql`:

```sql
CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY);
```

## Read it back

<Tabs syncKey="os">
<TabItem label="Linux and macOS">

```bash
cat schema.sql
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Windows PowerShell">

```powershell
Get-Content schema.sql
```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Expected output includes, on standard output:

```text
CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY);
```

## Say where it went

<Tabs syncKey="os">
<TabItem label="Linux and macOS">

```bash
ls schema.sql >&2
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Windows PowerShell">

```powershell
[Console]::Error.WriteLine('schema.sql')
```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Expected output includes, on standard error:

```text
schema.sql
```
